dataList.content:
And you're the one waiting for me round the clock this time!
这次是你对我翘首以盼了吗？

... Might you be talking to us?
……是在与我们说话吗？

<... She's Kromer's older sister. Her name's Kromer, too—just like her sister's.>
<……那个人是克罗默的姐姐。名字和妹妹一样，都是克罗默。>

The way she carries herself... Yeah, the resemblance is uncanny.
那种感觉……是的，错不了。

Seeing that happy-go-lucky grin on her face... something else fell into place.
看见这个笑眯眯看向我的人……我又察觉到了一件事。

Of course, she...
没错，那个人……

... She knew about the loop. She knew just how disappointed and hollow it'd left me feeling.
知道这个循环，也知道我的空虚感。

I strode up to Kromer, the sheer frustration dulling any reservation I may have had in the previous loops. Outis cried out in alarm as Sinclair drew a shocked gasp, but nothing was going to stop me now.
我大步向着那个人走去。虽然听见了奥提斯的惊愕声以及辛克莱那惊讶的呼吸声，但我并没有在意。

Whoa... Easy there—you're getting a bit too close for comfort. Don't want to push me into that same prosthesis-smashing frenzy zone my little sister fell into, do you?
哇啊……有点离得太近了吧？要是我像妹妹那样丧失判断力，一心沉溺于将你砸烂的话，你打算怎么办？

Huh? Is that... Meursault over there?
诶呀？那边……那个人，不正是默尔索先生吗？

I followed Hong Lu's finger... and found Meursault, no longer tied up in the Casualwear Hall. He'd probably rushed all the way to get here.
跟随着鸿璐手指的方向……我看见了不再困在快销服饰馆，而是赶到了这里来的默尔索。

<... Meursault.>
<……默尔索。>

Manager.
执行经理。

<I see you left the Casualwear Hall.>
<这次你不在快销服饰馆里了呢。>

Yes. I refused to remain in storage this time.
是，这次我拒绝了被保管。

<... Meursault, I need you to ask Kromer something.>
<……默尔索，问问那个人。>

< If she has a way to stop this, we need to know.>
<如果她知道停止的方法的话，希望她能告诉我们。>

What are you talking about? A way to stop what?
你们在说什么？关于什么的方法啊？

<She knows things about this place, Sinclair. And... I don't think she'll refuse to help us.>
<那个人知道关于这里的情报，辛克莱。另外……我觉得她不会拒绝帮助我们。>

I couldn't quite put a finger on why, but something told me that seeing us make progress was what she was here for, whatever that meant. She did help us on B2, after all.
虽然不清楚缘由，但那个人希望我们无论以何种形式都能继续前进。而实际上，她在B2F也帮助过我们。

... We request any information you might have...
……如果你知道其他方法的话……

... on how to change the outcome.
请你告诉我们。

... Now that's a huge letdown. Do I really have to spell it out for you?
……真让人失望啊？非要我特意说出来你们才懂吗？

I say this all the time, but if my sister lost to a company with this little going for it... then you did me a favor by getting rid of her. She'd only have become a dead weight on my future prospects later.
虽然我说过很多次了，但要是我的妹妹是败给了这种公司的话……你们还真是干得不错呢。反正她在之后也只会拖我的后腿吧。

Still not getting it?
还不懂吗？

Paradigm shift!
转换思维！

That's what you need right now.
正是你们现在所需要的啊。

"Boohoo, I've obediently followed the path laid before me by the Grand Magasin, and nothing's changed!" That's how you sound. Can't have your cake and eat it too, you know.
明明一直都在沿着百货店定好的路老老实实地走……却说什么不会改变，是不是太傲慢了点？

<The path laid by the Grand Magasin...>
<百货店定好的路……>

The first step in ushering in change is to break the established rules—and that's especially true for the Grand Magasin.
首先得打破既有的规则。要论起百货店的变化，就得在那之后吧？

So... Bash, smash, send the whole place crashing down. Just the way you dealt with my sister.
所以痛痛快快地破坏掉吧。就和你们对我妹妹做的一样。

Like the ones hiding in the shadows here, biding their time.
就在这里等待时机吧，像那些隐藏起来的人们一样。

<... So it was you. You are the Giant of Le Néant.>
<你，就是虚无派的巨人吧。>

<You're one of the four Giants holding this department store up.>
<背负百货店的四位巨人之一。>

Haha! Try speaking human next time, huh? Didn't get a single word of that ticking.
哈哈！我哪里知道你在说什么呢。

Well, I suppose I'll just take it as your undying gratitude that I'd stoop to helping a tin can like you.
就当你在发自内心地感激我愿意帮你这种义体家伙吧？

Why don't we meet again after you've broken the Grand Magasin's rules, hmm?
下次再见……就等你们帅气地打破百货店的规则之后吧……

And I expect nothing short of spectacular.
到时候再会了。

Of course, if you still can't make heads or tails of it...
哦，如果你们仍然不知所措的话……

Then just give up and stay here. Rot until you smell sweet and fertilize the Canned Experiences; at least you'll be of some use. If N Corp. can't change, it'd be better off dead. Euthanized.
就在这里……早点烂掉，成为经验罐头的材料吧。现如今的N公司，就这样慢慢死掉比较好吧。和安乐死一样。

Manager... You... How long have you known that woman?!
经理……那个人……您是什么时候认识她的？

<I met her only after we entered here, just as you all did.>
<来到这里才认识的。我和她初次见面的时间，和你们是一样的。>

<But... there are things we all went through that only Meursault and I remember.>
<然而……虽然大家都经历过，有些事情却只有我和默尔索记得。>

... Are you saying that our memories have been wiped... or were subjected to some equivalent procedure?
……也就是说，我们经历了记忆消除或者是类似的措施吗？

<... That's right.>
<……没错。>

I gave the Sinners an outline of how the whole system of Grand Magasin Sisyphe worked and brought them up to speed on how our past attempts ended.
我向罪人们介绍了西西弗百货的大概机制以及至今为止得到的结果。

At first, a few of them gave me that specific look that seemed to ask whether I'd lost my mind...
最开始我还能感受到在担心我的脑子是不是坏掉了的眼神……

But by the time I'd finished, the Sinners were all looking at me with complete trust.
但在全部说完后，罪人们的眼中产生了信任。

... We had no idea how much you'd gone through, Dante.
……真是辛苦您了，但丁阁下。

To have been of no assistance to you in such a grave predicament... I have no words, Executive Manager.
我竟未能在如此重大的事项中派上用场……实在惭愧。

If the lady in the restroom—I mean, the Fount—was telling the truth, you were supposed to keep this a secret even from us, weren't you?
卫生间……不，如果泉里那个人的话是真的，这件事也本应该对我们保密的吧。

I assume you've come up with another way this time around?
您是想出了什么其他方案了吗？

<No, not exactly...>
<不，虽然并非如此……>

<But we still have to find something else to try.>
<但，我们也得试着去寻找其他方法。>

We'd died countless deaths in this department store...
虽然我们在百货店内经验过无数次死亡……

But we'd also taken countless lives from those who lived here.
但相对地，我们也在百货店内夺去了无数条生命。

And sometimes... a being had appeared, a being who prevented us from killing certain entities, as though there were deaths he couldn't afford to let happen.
而在那之中……有时会出现似乎不希望某些人死去的存在。

<Whenever we tried to leave the path laid out for us...>
<每当我们就要偏离决定好的道路时……>

<Someone appeared to put things back the way they were.>
<会有存在将事物回归到原来的地方。>

Are you referring to... the Warden?
您是指……看守吗。

Every time the Warden killed Meursault and sent us back to the Fount, none of the other Sinners remembered anything about the encounter.
罪人中没有人记得看守的事情。

Which could only mean that being killed by him... was effectively the same thing as the two conclusions I'd gone through.
也就是说，被看守所杀死……和我所见过的两个结局没有区别。

<Yeah, every time the Warden appeared, he'd send things back into place. The extent of it was probably different each time, but it was—>
<一切都回归了原来的地方。或许范围有所不同，但那……>

... Similar to the Liquidation process you described.
……和执行经理所说的库存整理十分相似呢。

Based on the Executive Manager's account, this "Liquidation" process appears to be a form of hard reset, initiated when the Grand Magasin's Canned Experience output falls below the required threshold...
所谓的库存整理，根据执行经理的话语推测，似乎是在百货店的罐头产量达不到基准的情况下实行的一种强制重置……

... yet if a similar phenomenon can be triggered by the death of certain individuals in this place... I don't like what it might imply.
然而某些个体的死亡也会引起相似的现象……真是令人不安。

<Yeah, sounds like the Grand Magasin is nudging us to stick to its path...>
<百货店定好的路……>

<... If that's got anything to do with the Warden, maybe we could try defeating him...>
<如果能击败那个看守的话……>

<... and see if that stops those smaller Liquidations from happening. Maybe that'd allow us to make a different choice.>
<那种小规模的库存整理就不会发生，我们也许就能做出别的选择了。>

It will not be an easy battle, Manager.
恐怕不会是一场轻松的战斗。

<But what if... what if this choice isn't the solution either?>
<这个选择……如果也不是答案的话，该怎么办？>

For a moment, Meursault seemed unsure of how to reply.
默尔索似乎有些犹豫，像是在思考怎么回答。

Manager.
执行经理。

Are you afraid?
难道您在害怕吗？

<... Yeah. 'Course I am afraid.>
<……嗯，当然。>

<Always have been...>
<一直都是这样。>

<... and always will be, probably.>
<我觉得自己之后也会如此。>

I see.
是吗。

<Aren't you, Meursault?>
<默尔索，你不害怕吗？>

Fear arises from evaluating one's present circumstances. Therefore, if you cease to consider whether the present course is right or wrong and, by doing so, refrain from certainty...
恐惧产生于对现在的推测。因此，若要停止思考如今的对错，就必须保有确信……

... then you will be able to endure in spite of the fear.
那样即便恐惧也能忍受了。

You can then completely focus on what lies immediately before you.
如此便能只专注于眼前的事情。

<But by going down that path, wouldn't you eventually become...>
<但这样下去的话，迟早会……>

I didn't know how to answer what Meursault was telling me.
我不知道该如何回答这么说的默尔索。

<... too desensitized to even notice that you're hurting?>
<……连疼痛都感受不到了吧？>

The chains tightly binding my fists dull the pain from injuries.
我的拳头被锁链紧紧包裹，即便受伤，痛苦也会减轻。

That is another reason I coil the chains around me as an armor, Manager.
那是我将锁链作为铠甲缠绕的另一个理由，执行经理。

Meursault never seemed afraid or conflicted about anything.
默尔索从未表现出恐惧或是矛盾……

I couldn't really understand it, but it was something I'd envy from time to time.
那态度有时候会让我感到陌生，有时又会让我心生羡慕。

Fearlessness is an asset for people like us, after all—at times, Meursault even looked to be totally at ease no matter how daunting the mission was.
不会恐惧的人，在执行各种作战的时候都不会受阻，甚至看上去很轻松。

That said...
然而……

... I can say with certainty that there's been more to our journey than just fear.
话虽如此，我们并非一直处于恐惧之中。

When a mission finally went our way, or when we'd overcome impossible odds to reach what was expected of us... we'd celebrate together. We'd share the victory, and that gave us the strength to ready ourselves for the next ordeal sure to come.
在作战最终顺利进行，我们克服困难终于达成目标的时候……我们会一起分享胜利的喜悦，并准备着迎接一定会到来的下一次困难。

And I realize that Meursault had never been a part of it.
而在那过程之中，默尔索也总是向后退去。

He'd always maintained his distance, unable to share even those brief moments of joy and respite together.
短暂的喜悦也好，休息也罢，都没有一起共享。

<When the going gets tough... I just allow myself to feel weary.>
<我……在难受的时候就会感到难受，>

<And when I'm scared, well... I just I say that I'm scared.>
<害怕的时候就会说自己在害怕。>

<And... I'm going to keep doing that.>
<而且……之后我也会这么做。>

Has doing so... brought about any meaningful change?
那样的行为……会带来什么显著的改变吗？

My answer was pathetic.
我的回答很粗糙。

<For now... Let's head to 2F.>
<总之……先去2F吧。>

But even if it turns out nothing's going to change, we still have to keep climbing.
但即便什么也不会改变，我们也必须向上走。
